title: Build a Second Brain with AI and Notion (Step by Step)

scenes.chapterTitle: Intro: up to 2 hours a day, just searching
scenes.badge: Workers who waste up to 2 hours a day finding information
scenes.sub: Lucid poll of 2,000+ knowledge workers (UK), May 2025
scenes.text: More than half of office workers, fifty three percent, say they waste up to two hours a day just trying to find the information they need for their job. That's from a poll of more than two thousand knowledge workers by the software company Lucid, reported in May twenty twenty five. The fix isn't a better memory. It's a second brain: one trusted place for your notes, ideas and files. In this video, I'll show you how to build one in Notion with AI, step by step. The structure, the setup, the exact prompts, what's free, and the mistakes to avoid.

scenes.chapterTitle: The plan: Notion stores, AI sorts, you decide
scenes.title: Your second brain in one afternoon
scenes.sub: Notion stores it. AI does the busy work. You decide.
scenes.text: Here's the promise. By the end of this video, you'll know how to set up a working second brain in one afternoon. Notion is the storage: pages and databases where everything lives. AI does the busy work: sorting, summarizing and finding things. And you make the decisions. One honest note before we start: a second brain only helps if you use it. So we'll keep the system small, simple, and built around the work you're doing right now, not around collecting more stuff.

scenes.chapterTitle: What a second brain really is

items.text: What do I do with it?

scenes.text: So what is a second brain, really? It's a system that answers three questions without you thinking hard. One: where do I put this new idea, link or file? Two: where did I save that thing I need right now? Three: what do I actually do with it? Most note apps fail on the first question. Everything goes into one giant list, and finding it later becomes the two hour problem. The structure we'll use fixes that, and it's called PARA.

items.name: Projects
items.desc: Short-term, with a goal and an end

footer.text: Sort by what it's for, not by subject

scenes.text: PARA comes from productivity writer Tiago Forte, the author of Building a Second Brain. It sorts everything into four groups, based on how actionable it is. Projects are short-term efforts with a clear goal and an end, like launching a website. Areas are parts of your life or work that need ongoing attention, like health, finances or a client. Resources are topics you're interested in or learning about. And Archives hold anything that's no longer active but that you might want later. The trick is to sort by what you're using it for, not by subject.

scenes.chapterTitle: Set it up in Notion in 4 steps

items.text: One Notes database + a Type property

scenes.text: Now let's build it in Notion. Step one: create a page called Inbox. Everything new lands here first, with no sorting. Step two: create one database called Notes, with a property called Type that has four options: Project, Area, Resource and Archive. One database is easier to search than four separate pages. Step three: add a Status property, so you can mark each note as new, in use, or done. Step four: create a Projects database and link each note to the project it supports. That's the whole skeleton, and you can build it in one sitting.

Next, capture. The rule is simple: saving something should take less than ten seconds, or you won't do it. On a computer, use the free Notion Web Clipper to send any article straight to your Inbox. On your phone, use the share button and pick Notion. For your own ideas, keep a quick note open and type one line. Don't sort while you capture. Don't add tags yet. Just get it in. Sorting is a separate job, and that's where AI comes in.

scenes.chapterTitle: Let AI sort your inbox (the prompt)

items.text: Give AI your projects and areas
Ask: which PARA group + one-line reason

scenes.text: Once a week, let AI sort your Inbox. If you pay for Notion AI, open the Inbox and ask it there. If you don't, copy the titles into any free chatbot, like ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini. Use this prompt: here are my current projects and areas. For each item below, suggest Project, Area, Resource or Archive, and give a one line reason. Then check the list and move each note yourself. AI suggests, you decide. It's fast, because AI does the thinking you'd normally put off, and you still catch the ones it gets wrong.

Saving an article isn't the same as learning from it. So for anything long, ask AI for a short summary you can read in thirty seconds. Here's a prompt that works: summarize this in three bullet points, list one action I could take, and one question it leaves open. Paste the answer at the top of the note, above the original. Months later, you'll read the summary instead of the whole page. One warning: AI summaries can miss things or get details wrong, so check numbers and quotes against the source before you use them.

scenes.chapterTitle: What Notion AI costs (and the free route)
scenes.text: What does this cost? Notion's Free plan costs zero dollars, but it only includes a limited trial of Notion AI. Plus is ten dollars per member a month on a yearly plan, or twelve billed monthly, and it still only gets the AI trial. Business is twenty dollars a month yearly, or twenty four monthly, and that's the plan that includes Notion AI, with monthly AI credits for each member. So for one person, Notion AI means about two hundred forty dollars a year. Or you can stay free and use a free chatbot instead. Prices checked November twenty twenty six.

chips.text: Big files: paste a cloud link
Free chatbot for the AI part

scenes.text: And for most people, the Free plan is enough to start. For one person, pages and blocks are unlimited. The limits: files you upload can be up to five megabytes each, page history only goes back seven days, and you can invite up to ten guests. For a personal second brain, that's usually fine. Store big files, like videos, in your cloud drive and paste the link into Notion. So the free route is Notion Free plus a free chatbot for sorting and summaries. Upgrade only if copying and pasting starts costing you real time.

scenes.chapterTitle: 5 mistakes that kill a second brain

items.name: Hoarding
items.desc: A note that never helps is clutter

items.name: Tag overload
items.desc: 4 types and a status are enough

items.name: Private data
items.desc: No passwords, client data, medical info

items.name: Blind trust
items.desc: Summaries can sound sure and be wrong

footer.text: Save time, don't create a second job

scenes.text: Now the five mistakes that kill most second brains. One: building the perfect system before saving anything. Start simple. Two: collecting without using. If a note never helps a project, it's clutter. Three: too many tags. Four types and a status are enough. Four: pasting private things into AI, like passwords, client data or medical details. Check your company's rules first. And five: trusting AI summaries blindly. They can sound sure and still be wrong. Your second brain should save you time, not become a second job.

items.text: Use one saved note this week

scenes.text: Finally, the habit that keeps it alive: a fifteen minute weekly review. First, empty your Inbox: let AI suggest where each note goes, then move it. Second, update your projects: mark what's done and add what's new. Third, move finished projects and their notes to Archive, so your active lists stay short. And last, pick one saved note and actually use it this week, in an email, a plan or a decision. That last step is the whole point. A second brain isn't a library. It's a tool for getting work done.

scenes.title: Build it this weekend
scenes.next: Emergency Fund: How Much You Really Need
scenes.text: So that's the system. Capture fast into an Inbox, sort with PARA, let AI suggest and summarize, and review once a week. Start with the free plan and a free chatbot, and upgrade only if you need to. What's the one thing you always lose and have to search for? Tell me in the comments. I read them. If this helped, subscribe to Future Money Lab. Next up, emergency funds: how much you really need, and where to keep it.

This is a step-by-step guide to building a second brain in Notion with AI: Tiago Forte's PARA structure (Projects, Areas, Resources, Archives), a simple 4-step Notion setup with one database, capturing in under 10 seconds, prompts to let AI sort your inbox and summarize long notes, what Notion AI costs vs the free route, the Free plan limits, 5 mistakes to avoid, and a 15-minute weekly review.
youtube.details:
Numbers mentioned (checked November 2026; plans change often, always confirm on Notion's official pricing page):
- 53% of workers waste up to two hours a day trying to find information they need for their job; poll of more than 2,000 knowledge workers by Lucid (UK-focused), reported by Personnel Today, May 6, 2025.
- PARA (Projects, Areas, Resources, Archives) is a framework by Tiago Forte, author of Building a Second Brain; definitions paraphrased from Taskade's guide.
- Notion plans per member: Free $0; Plus $10/month billed yearly or $12 monthly; Business $20/month billed yearly or $24 monthly; Enterprise custom. Free and Plus get only a limited Notion AI trial; Business includes Notion AI with monthly credits per member (1,500 Standard + 500 Select per the sources) (Breeze, Sep 2026; Dupple, Oct 2026).
- '$240 a year' = $20 x 12 months for one Business member, billed yearly.
- Notion Free plan: unlimited pages and blocks for one person, files up to 5 MB each, 7 days of page history, up to 10 guests (Dupple, Oct 2026).
- The prompts and the weekly review are our own suggested workflow, not measured results.
